# Worst period (`worst_period`)

*Category: Return summary · Nature: observed · Unit: decimal_return · Formula id: `worst_period@v1` · Methodology 0.1.0*

## 1. What does it measure?

Lowest single-period return in the history.

## 2. Formula

```text
min(r_t)
```

## 3. Required inputs

Periodic simple returns.

## 4. Is higher or lower better?

Higher is better.

## 5. Plain-language interpretation

The worst single period (e.g. month) the investment had.

## 6. Professional interpretation

Observed lower extreme; a model-free loss statistic that is always shown.

## 7. Assumptions

- None beyond the general inputs.

## 8. When can it be misleading?

- Histories of different lengths are compared; longer histories tend to contain worse periods.

## 9. Minimum sensible data

Any non-empty history. (policy `observed_point`: Observed fact about the supplied history; any non-empty history suffices.)

## 10. Reference implementations

| Library | Function | Agrees | Note |
|---|---|---|---|

| NumPy | `min` | yes |  |

## 11. Sources

- Bacon, C. R. (2021). Practical Risk-Adjusted Performance Measurement (2nd ed.). Wiley.

## 12. OpenFactsheet convention

Per observation period; signed (negative = loss).
